subsystems.name: Data capture
subsystems.role: records how the expert works, so their decisions can be learned.

subsystems.name: Knowledge structuring
subsystems.role: turns raw records into a usable representation of the expert's expertise.

subsystems.name: Base model
subsystems.role: provides general language and reasoning ability before specialization.
parts: vision or multimodal model if needed

subsystems.name: Fine-tuning and alignment
subsystems.role: shapes the model to think like the specific expert.

subsystems.name: Action and tool use
subsystems.role: lets the proxy perform tasks, not just talk.

subsystems.name: Verification and oversight
subsystems.role: checks that the proxy behaves like the expert and catches errors.
parts: automated tests against held-out expert decisions

buildSteps.title: Choose the expert and scope
buildSteps.detail: Select a person whose decisions are valuable and a narrow task, such as triaging support tickets or reviewing loan applications.

buildSteps.title: Capture their working life
buildSteps.detail: Record their screens, emails, meetings, written notes and the decisions they make, with consent and privacy safeguards.

buildSteps.title: Label decisions and outcomes
buildSteps.detail: For each captured decision, note the context, the choice made, and what happened later, so the model can learn cause and effect.

buildSteps.title: Train a base model on general data
buildSteps.detail: Start from a large language model that already understands language and basic reasoning.

buildSteps.title: Specialise the model
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune it on the expert's labelled decisions, then use reinforcement learning from the expert's corrections to match their judgement.

buildSteps.title: Test against the expert
buildSteps.detail: Give the model unseen cases and compare its choices with the expert's; iterate until it agrees on most routine decisions.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with limits
buildSteps.detail: Run it as a suggestion tool first, with the expert or a colleague approving every action, and expand autonomy only as trust and accuracy grow.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with reliable reasoning
prerequisites.why: current models can mimic style and recall facts, but still make errors and cannot truly replicate expert intuition.

prerequisites.tech: Comprehensive data capture from expert work
prerequisites.why: logging tools exist, but capturing the full context of a person's decisions over years is invasive and incomplete.

prerequisites.tech: Methods to measure fidelity to a person's judgement
prerequisites.why: there is no standard test for whether a model thinks like a specific human, only tests of general accuracy.
techniques like differential privacy and federated learning exist, but not at the scale needed for a lifetime of personal data.
APIs and guardrails are emerging, but letting an AI act autonomously in the real world remains risky.

pathway.milestone: AI assistants that summarise, draft and retrieve information under human direction
domain-specific expert copilots that suggest decisions and learn from feedback
pathway.unlocks: narrow, supervised automation of routine expert tasks.

pathway.milestone: digital twins of specific experts that pass routine cases with human oversight
pathway.unlocks: scaling a single expert's judgement to many places at once.

pathway.milestone: autonomous proxies that handle complex, novel cases with accountability
pathway.unlocks: remote expertise as a service, if trust and verification are solved.
